title: App code
description: How the web app's code is written, so that every page and every agent's change reads the same way and stays easy to change: where layout and style live, colors as tokens, generic components, labels, accessible names, spelling and addresses. The app lives in `app/src`; Platform (`LA-PLT`) follows this pattern for all of it, and holds the tests that prove it for the whole app. How the app behaves for the person using it (hover, the workbench, the page bar, motion, row links, addresses, touch and stability) is the App experience pattern, `LA-PAT-APP-UX`.
notes:
The rules come from problems the app has had: a button laid over a heading with CSS that overlapped the list below it, a page style that reached every `header` element, "Capabilitys" from a hand-made plural, and spelling that drifted between British and American.

## How a domain uses the pattern

The domain links the pattern with `follows`. The pattern has no settings: every rule applies to all of the domain's code. Each rule is proved by a test in `app/test` (most in `standards.test.tsx`) that reads the source or renders the main pages, and that names the file and line to fix when it fails. R21's tests also run knip on the app, the engine and the desktop app. Its rules are pattern rules, not standard rules, because tests prove them: a rule you prove with tests is a pattern rule, and a rule you follow and meet is a standard rule. The rules the engine's code follows and meets are the standard `LA-STD-CODE`.

## Rules

- `LA-PAT-APP-CODE-R01`: layout lives in the markup.
- `LA-PAT-APP-CODE-R02`: styles are set by class.
- `LA-PAT-APP-CODE-R03`: colors and shadows are tokens.
- `LA-PAT-APP-CODE-R04`: generic components know nothing of specs.
- `LA-PAT-APP-CODE-R05`: kind labels become plural only through `plural()`, and lowercase only through `lowerLabel()`.
- `LA-PAT-APP-CODE-R06`: every control has an accessible name.
- `LA-PAT-APP-CODE-R07`: American spelling.
- `LA-PAT-APP-CODE-R10`: every grid says its columns.
- `LA-PAT-APP-CODE-R15`: themes only set tokens.
- `LA-PAT-APP-CODE-R19`: one address per thing, made by `addressOf`.
- `LA-PAT-APP-CODE-R20`: changes are hard cutovers, with no compatibility layer.
- `LA-PAT-APP-CODE-R21`: nothing outlives its purpose: no unused code, style, command or icon, and every mark the Graph and Model views draw is in their key.

The numbers of the rules that moved to App experience (R08, R09, R11 to R14, R16 and R17) are not reused; new rules here continue from R22.

title: App experience
description: How the web app behaves for the person using it, so that every page feels the same to the hand and the eye: what shows a hover, how the workbench's panels sit and resize, what the page bar and each pane's header hold, how things move, how a row leads to its record and a card takes its one action, how every open thing keeps an address, how it all works by touch, that nothing jumps, that actions look like actions, and that it stays within its performance budgets. The app lives in `app/src`; Platform (`LA-PLT`) follows this pattern for all of it, and holds the tests that prove it for the whole app. How the code itself is written (layout in markup, classes, tokens, generic components, labels, names and spelling) is the App code pattern, `LA-PAT-APP-CODE`.
notes:
## How a domain uses the pattern

The domain links the pattern with `follows`. The pattern has no settings: every rule applies to all of the domain's pages. Each rule is proved by a test in `app/test` that reads the source or renders the main pages, and that names the file and line to fix when it fails. `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R08` is proved in a real browser by the stability suite (`app/stability`, `npm --prefix app run test:stability`), and at the source by `app/test/nothing-jumps.test.tsx`. `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R11` is proved on the production build by the performance suite (`app/perf`, `npm --prefix app run test:perf`). `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R10` is proved in a real browser by the accessibility suite (`app/a11y`, `npm --prefix app run test:a11y`). `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R12` is proved by a sweep over the repo's own specs in the unit run and in a real browser by the stability suite.

## Rules

- `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R01`: everything clickable shows a hover state.
- `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R02`: the workbench, panels a gap apart and every gap resizes.
- `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R03`: the page bar holds the page's tabs and layout controls; each pane's header holds only that pane's actions.
- `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R04`: motion is shared and optional.
- `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R05`: a row that leads to one record is one link.
- `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R06`: every open thing has an address.
- `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R07`: everything works by touch.
- `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R08`: nothing jumps.
- `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R09`: actions look like actions.
- `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R10`: every page passes the accessibility audit.
- `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R11`: Lathe stays within its performance budgets.
- `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R12`: every drawn box shows its name.
- `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R13`: labels read in sentence case.
- `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R14`: a card has one primary action, taken by clicking anywhere on it.

New rules continue from UX-R15.
